name: Variable-temperature 57Fe Mossbauer spectroscopy (140 K to <=5 K) of 57Fe-labelled ferrihydrite transformation in anoxic paddy-soil incubations
plain_name: Track how iron rust minerals change in soil by cooling them toward 5 K for gamma-ray spectra
description: 57Fe-ferrihydrite (65 mg) is mixed into 15 g of soil and incubated anoxically; solids are frozen in liquid nitrogen, freeze-dried and measured by 57Fe Mossbauer spectroscopy at 140, 77, 45, 25, 15, 10 and <=5 K, because magnetic ordering of ferrihydrite and secondary Fe(II)/Fe(III) phases only appears at the lowest temperatures.
keywords: Track how iron rust minerals change in soil by cooling them toward 5 K for gamma-ray spectra

sources.citation: Notini et al. (2023) A New Approach for Investigating Iron Mineral Transformations in Soils and Sediments Using 57Fe-Labeled Minerals and 57Fe Mossbauer Spectroscopy, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57, 10008-10018, doi:10.1021/acs.est.3c00434

reported_equipment: MBraun anoxic glovebox (N2 atmosphere, <5 ppm O2)
57Fe Mossbauer spectrometer and cryostat (models given only in the Supporting Information, not in the main text)

requirements.rationale: The temperature profile runs from 140 K down to 5 K; the cryostat must cover this whole window.
The Fe(II) octet only forms below 15 K and the decisive spectra were taken at <=5 K.
Routine incubation-series spectra were collected at 77 K.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
